answer: Anchor each agent to one aged social account. First, the agent binds an account two years old with 500 posts, and the platform attests its age. Second, one account anchors one agent, and a second binding is rejected. Third, every quarter the registry asks for a post within 24 hours, and a miss freezes the identity. Buying 1,000 aged accounts costs 300 dollars each, so 300,000 dollars, and bought ones get banned fast. A fresh account starts at its nadir. Two years of posts are a beacon, and one fake sends a ripple the registry spots at once. Trust at its zenith is built post by post.
